page.title: Box destination
page.subtitle: Backup snapshots are written to the Box folder ID you specify. Use folder_id "0" for the account root.
page.registerHint: This plugin owns one LocationType: box. To change the folder later, save the destination and re-open it.

help.clientId: Client ID from the Box Developer Console for your app (Custom App or Server Authentication).
help.clientSecret: Client Secret from the Box Developer Console. Treated as a write-only secret; the plugin never logs it back.
help.folderId: Box folder ID where backups land. Use "0" for the account root.
help.refreshToken: Long-lived refresh token issued after the OAuth consent flow. Leave empty until you have run Connect to Box.

help.clientId: From the Box Developer Console: App → Configuration → OAuth 2.0.
help.clientSecret: The Client Secret is shown once when the app is created — copy it now.
help.folderId: Numeric Box folder ID. "0" = the account root. Find a folder's ID in the Box web UI URL.
help.refreshToken: Filled in automatically by the Connect to Box flow. Do not edit manually.
help.oauthHint: After saving, click "Connect to Box" to grant the plugin consent and store a refresh token. Without a refresh token the plugin falls back to client_credentials grant (requires Server Authentication configured on the Box app).

setup.title: Box setup guide
setup.subtitle: Wire a Box developer app to your McHarbor instance in six short steps. About 5 minutes.

step1.title: Create a Box app
step1.body: Open the Box Developer Console (developer.box.com) and create a new app. Choose "Custom App" for delegated user auth, or "Server Authentication" if you prefer app-only tokens (no per-user consent).

step2.title: Configure OAuth 2.0
step2.body: In the app settings, choose OAuth 2.0. Add the redirect URI your McHarbor instance serves (Settings → Storage → Connect to Box will display it). Pick a single primary environment for now (development or production).

step3.title: Request scopes
step3.body: Under "Application Scopes", enable file_readwrite (full read/write on all files and folders the user can access). Older apps may still use root_readwrite — both work with this plugin.

step4.title: Submit app for authorization
step4.body: Custom Apps require a Box admin to authorize the app before users can grant consent. Have your Box admin click the "Authorize" button in the Developer Console, then approve the requested scopes.

step5.title: Copy client_id + client_secret
step5.body: Back in McHarbor, paste the Client ID and Client Secret from the Box Developer Console into the destination form. Save the destination before proceeding.

step6.title: Connect to grant consent
step6.body: Open the saved destination and click "Connect to Box". The plugin launches the OAuth consent flow against Box; after consent, Box redirects back with an authorization code that the host exchanges for a long-lived refresh token (stored encrypted in the destination).

setup.footer: Need folder-level scoping instead of account-wide? Use a Service Account scoped to a Box folder and paste the Service Account credentials into the destination form. The plugin uses whatever credentials are present at runtime.

toast.oauthGranted: Box account connected. Refresh token stored.
toast.oauthDenied: Box authorization denied. Connect again to retry.

error.tokenFailed: Could not exchange credentials for a Box access token. Verify client_id + client_secret and try again.
